newsitem.title: USA: 17 accused in big holdup of U.S. computer company.
newsitem.headline: 17 accused in big holdup of U.S. computer company.

text.p: Seventeen suspects linked to Asian organised crime in the United States have been indicted in connection with the largest U.S. robbery of a computer company, the federal prosecutor's office said on Monday.

Nine of the 17 were arrested early on Monday, said a spokesman for Nora Manella, the U.S. Attorney for the central district of California. Two were ethnic Chinese, one was Cambodian and 14 were of Vietnamese origin, he said.

"All are linked to Asian street gangs (in the United States) or larger organised crime enterprises," the spokesman said. He added there was no indication the robbery had been ordered by crime syndicates in Hong Kong or Vietnam.

The 17 were charged with robbing Centon Electronics in Irvine, California, of $10 million in computer chips and motherboards in May 1995. The crime was believed to be the largest computer business robbery in U.S. history, the spokesman said.

The four-count indictment also charged 11 of the suspects in connection with another robbery, in which $400,000 worth of chips were taken. All 17 were accused of using firearms in committing the crimes.
They face maximum sentences of 40 years in prison for the robberies and an additional 25 years for the use of firearms.
The indictment is the result of a coordinated effort between law enforcement agencies in California and Portland, Oregon.
Last year 24 suspects were indicted in the case in San Francisco, and 20 were indicted in San Jose. Earlier this year, another nine suspects were indicted in Portland.
